page.layout: One printed page. Top left: page number. Top centre: running head "EMBLEMA". Below it, a centred heading "MORS ÆQVAT OMNIA." Then a framed engraving of a skeleton holding scales, with a naked man below. Under the engraving, four centred lines of italic verse. Bottom right: a catchword "Mors".

p.i: Pallida per similli mors trutinat omnia lance:
Quæq; subis hodie, cras ego forte luo.
Chara fides semper pectora nostra regant.

page.notes: The engraving shows a skeleton holding two skulls and a balance with hourglasses; the pans hold skulls and heads, and below stands a naked man on the ground. It is not transcribed as text. The verse line 1 has "similli" as printed (possibly "simili"). The Greek word in line 3 is printed small and may be read imperfectly; "Αὐτάρκεια" is a best reading. The "&" in line 3 is the printed ampersand.
